Worktree `feat/empty-defaults-config-file`.

- **2026-08-24 (config UI consolidation — one provider surface, one chain editor):** Killed two redundancies. (1) Each provider now renders **once** in the Providers & Models catalog: the standalone "Provider Key Configs" grid was folded into the per-provider group headers (key pill + env var + Configure/Update key + Reset key + 🔄 Fetch live + Edit/Delete for custom providers), and per-provider live-model fetch now populates the group's own list — the same list you toggle (auto-saved), search (global + per-provider), and stage from via **＋ Fallback** (header shows `matched/total · N served`). (2) Fallback chain editing exists **only** on the Fallback Routes page: the Providers-page chain selector, drag-order panel, and per-row fallback checkboxes were removed; **＋ Fallback** hands a model to `/config/fallback?add=<id>` which pre-stages it into the selected chain (existing chains auto-save; a "chain" query param can preselect a chain). Dead JS removed (live-block subsystem, providers-page chain panel, dual-list drag paths) and the duplicate `#message` div dropped. Worktree `feat/config-ui-consolidation`.

- **2026-08-24 (IDE version compat + chain configs + unified Providers page):** Four fixes in one worktree. (1) **VS Code "Unable to verify Ollama server version" hardening:** `GET /api/version` now mirrors the real backend ollama's version (30s cache; `OLLAMA_VERSION` env still overrides; `0.6.4` floor), and the server dual-binds `127.0.0.1` + `::1` so `localhost` resolution order can't surface a false ECONNREFUSED version error; Providers page gains an IDE-compatibility explainer (`chat.byok.ollamaEndpoint` → `http://localhost:11434`) and the sidebar badge now shows the mirrored version live. (2) **Add-Model dropdown source fix:** the Fallback Routes "Add Model to Chain" dropdown now lists the full toggle catalog (`/api/model-curation`, same inventory chain validation accepts — 1807 ids live vs the 7 the curated `/api/tags` served), with in-chain ✓ marks and ctx/out/tools/vision spec chips; previously fallback-toggled-but-not-served models were invisible. (3) **Chain configs exposed:** `GET /api/fallback-models` returns per-route `chainDetails` (provider, context/output sizes, capability flags, `known`/`served`, key-readiness `status`); `/api/show` for `local-router/*` returns `local_router_chain` + `model_info['local-router.chain']`; both config pages render per-step specs and readiness tooltips. (4) **Providers page unified:** "Provider Key Configs" merged into the "Available Providers & Models" card (now "Providers, Keys & Models") — one card covers key status grid, curation catalog (each provider group header shows its key pill + env var + Configure-key shortcut to the key form), and the fallback chain panel. Worktree `fix/config-ui-ollama-compat`.

- **2026-08-23 (curation configs + registry-scoped validation):** Providers & Models gains **Select all** / **Deselect all** bulk curation controls and **named curation configs** — save the current selection as a named config, load it, delete it, and mark one as the default (re-applied at every boot). Backend: `curation-configs.json` + `GET/POST/DELETE /api/curation-configs`, `POST /api/curation-configs/load`, `PUT /api/curation-configs/default`. Chain authoring now takes inventory scope: `allCatalogModels()` unions the static provider registry with the live cache, so registry-known steps (e.g. `zai-code-pass-glm-5.1`, `openrouter-chain-of-draft`) pass fallback reference validation — Edit → Save on preset chains works again even when the serving curation is narrow or empty. Worktree `feat/curation-config-presets`.

- **2026-08-23 (headroom 0.36.5 + per-provider caching docs):** Upgraded `headroom-ai` from `^0.22.4` to `^0.36.5` (latest, released 2026-08-22). The `compress(messages, { model, baseUrl, timeout, fallback, retries, stack })` API is backward-compatible — no call-site changes required; `tsc` clean and all 9 headroom tests pass. Added `docs/caching/<provider>.txt` — 21 plain-text docs (one per registry provider, incl. `openrouter-presets`), each a researched, source-cited snapshot of that provider's maximum prompt/context caching: mechanism type, max TTL, breakpoint caps, minimum token thresholds, cache read/write pricing, a maxing recipe, and how local-router's `injectPromptCaching` leverages it. Every file stamped "Last verified: 2026-08-23" with source URLs. Worktree `chore/headroom-caching-docs`.

- **2026-08-20 (PQC native ML-KEM):** Synced the Python PQC engine migration from ainish-coder (617163b): keygen/encapsulate/decapsulate now use native `cryptography>=45` ML-KEM-768; new keygens store the FIPS 203 seed form (64 bytes); legacy 2400-byte expanded-form stores remain readable via a lazy kyber-py fallback that prints a rotation hint. Bundle JSON layout unchanged, Rust-engine interoperable, new bundles tagged `engine=py-native-mlkem`. Verified live on :11436 against the real bundle. Worktree `feat/pqc-native-mlkem-sync`.

- **2026-08-20 (config-ui cache):** Browsers heuristically cached `/config` HTML (no Cache-Control header was sent), so after a server restart or port rebind the browser could serve a stale page that stalled forever at "Loading catalog..." while every API endpoint was healthy. Added `Cache-Control: no-store` to the `/config` redirect and all six config pages — they render live state (keys, catalog, routes) and must never be cached. Worktree `fix/config-ui-cache`.

- **2026-06-13 (headroom integration):** Integrated [Headroom](https://github.com/chopratejas/headroom) (`headroom-ai` npm package) as a toggleable context compression layer. Added `headroom-config.json` config file (`{ enabled, proxyUrl }`) with load/persist/toggle following the Wafer ZDR pattern. Wired `compressWithHeadroom()` into the `proxyModelAttempt` pipeline between `sanitizeProviderRequestBody` and `injectPromptCaching` — the compression reduces tokens before cache directives are injected, so both layers are complementary. Added `GET/PUT /api/headroom-config` routes, `ConfigApiDeps` interface extension, configState getter/setter, and startup log message. Enabled by default; graceful degradation if the Headroom proxy (`http://localhost:8787`) is unreachable. Added Headroom Context Compression toggle card to the `/config` UI and added support for `deepseek-v4-pro` in the Wafer ZDR eligibility list (updating both UI and backend). Added 8 test cases in `tests/headroom-compression.test.mjs` and an end-to-end integration test in `tests/headroom-integration.test.mjs`.

## Provider Integration Research — OAuth / Subscription Providers (June 2026)

Research into integrating two new provider types that use OAuth authentication instead of static API keys: **Google Antigravity** and **GitHub Copilot**. These are subscription-based providers with quota-limited access. The goal is to add them as first-class providers in the Local Router catalog alongside the existing 15 static-key providers.

### Why These Providers

Both Antigravity and GitHub Copilot offer access to frontier models (Claude, GPT, Gemini) through a single subscription, making them high-value additions to the Local Router provider catalog. Unlike current providers that use static API keys, these require OAuth flows with short-lived tokens and automatic refresh.

### Provider 1: Google Antigravity (Subscription / Quota-Limited)

**Product Overview:**
- Google Antigravity is an agent-based AI development platform launched November 2025 (VS Code-based, built by the ex-Windsurf team acquired for $2.4B).
- At Google I/O May 2026, it expanded to a five-surface platform: Antigravity 2.0 (desktop), Antigravity CLI (`agy`), Antigravity SDK, Managed Agents API, and Enterprise.
- Replaced Gemini CLI (shutdown June 18, 2026). CLI binary is Go-based, invoked as `agy`.
- Built-in models: Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 3 Flash, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-OSS 120B.
- Pricing: Free ($0, 20 req/day, Gemini Flash only), AI Pro ($20/mo, 1,000 credits), AI Ultra ($250/mo, 25,000 credits).
- Uses a hybrid quota system: sprint quota (5-hour refresh) + weekly baseline cap + AI credits for overage.

**Authentication Flow — OAuth 2.0 with PKCE:**
1. Client generates PKCE verifier/challenge pair (SHA-256 + base64url).
2. Opens browser to Google OAuth authorization URL: `https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth`
3. Required OAuth scopes: `cloud-platform`, `userinfo.email`, `userinfo.profile`, `cclog`, `experimentsandconfigs`
4. Redirect URI: local HTTP server (e.g. `http://localhost:51121/oauth-callback`) or manual paste for headless.
5. Exchange authorization code for tokens at `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token` (includes `client_id`, `client_secret`, PKCE `code_verifier`).
6. Access token + refresh token returned. Access token is short-lived; refresh token is long-lived.
7. Auto-refresh: when access token expires, use refresh token to get a new one at the same token endpoint.

**API Surface:**
- OpenAI-compatible chat completions format.
- Model discovery via API (dynamic model list).
- Streaming SSE support.
- Usage/quota tracking via response headers or separate API.
- Version override available: `PI_AI_ANTIGRAVITY_VERSION` env var.

**Implementation Notes for Local Router:**
- Provider ID: `antigravity` (slug).
- Key env var: `ANTIGRAVITY_OAUTH_TOKEN` (but token is short-lived, needs refresh).
- The token lifecycle management is fundamentally different from static-key providers. The Local Router key store (`keyStore`) currently assumes static strings. We need a new `OAuthProviderState` that stores `{ accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAt }` per provider and a background refresh timer.
- The `/config` UI needs an "OAuth Login" button (opens browser to Google auth flow) instead of a text field for API key entry.
- The `POST /api/keys` endpoint needs a new branch for OAuth providers that stores the initial token set instead of a plain API key.
- New module needed: `src/oauth-providers.ts` — handles PKCE generation, local callback server, token exchange, auto-refresh, and credential persistence.
- The PQC bundle must store OAuth tokens (access + refresh + expiry) alongside static API keys. The existing `secrets.bundle.json` format can be extended with a per-provider `authType: 'oauth' | 'static'` discriminator.
- Quota awareness: Antigravity has strict quota limits. The Local Router routing logic should be extended to track quota exhaustion per-provider (detect 429 responses or quota-specific error codes) and temporarily deprioritize or skip the provider.

**Reference Implementations:**
- `oh-my-pi` / `pi-mono` (upstream): `npx @mariozechner/pi-ai login google-antigravity` — full OAuth PKCE flow with `loginAntigravity()` function. Uses `auth.json` for credential persistence. Auto-refresh via `getOAuthApiKey('google-antigravity', auth)`. ([mintlify.wiki/badlogic/pi-mono/ai/oauth](https://mintlify.wiki/badlogic/pi-mono/ai/oauth))
- `opencode-google-antigravity-auth` plugin: PKCE flow, multi-account load balancing (up to 10 Google accounts), automatic rate-limit detection and account switching, streaming response transformation, thinking block extraction. ([deepwiki.com/shekohex/opencode-google-antigravity-auth](https://deepwiki.com/shekohex/opencode-google-antigravity-auth/6.3-api-endpoints-and-constants))
- PicoClaw: Complete Antigravity auth guide with PKCE implementation, token management, model fetching, usage tracking. ([docs.picoclaw.io/docs/providers/antigravity](https://docs.picoclaw.io/docs/providers/antigravity/))
- `oh-my-opencode` / `fractalmind-ai`: Internal auth component integrating with `opencode-antigravity-auth` plugin for multi-account Gemini access. ([deepwiki.com/fractalmind-ai/oh-my-opencode/8.6-google-antigravity-authentication](https://deepwiki.com/fractalmind-ai/oh-my-opencode/8.6-google-antigravity-authentication))

### Provider 2: GitHub Copilot (Subscription / Quota-Limited)

**Product Overview:**
- GitHub Copilot exposes a standard OpenAI-style endpoint at `https://api.githubcopilot.com`.
- Subscription includes access to multiple frontier models: Claude (Sonnet, Opus), GPT (4o, 4.1, 5.x), Gemini, o-series — all through a single API.
- Copilot CLI provides `copilot login` — OAuth device flow authentication.
- Tokens are short-lived (~30 minutes). Must be refreshed by re-exchanging the GitHub OAuth token for a new Copilot API token.

**Authentication Flow — OAuth Device Flow (RFC 8628):**
1. CLI requests device code from `https://github.com/login/device/code` (well-known public Copilot client ID: `Iv1.b507a08c87ecfe98`).
2. User visits `https://github.com/login/device` and enters the short code displayed in the terminal.
3. CLI polls `https://github.com/github/login/oauth/access_token` until the user authorizes.
4. GitHub token (`ghu_...` or `gho_...`) is exchanged for a short-lived Copilot API token via `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` with `Authorization: token <github_token>`.
5. Response: `{ "token": "tid=...", "expires_at": "..." }`.
6. The Copilot API token (~30 min lifetime) is used as bearer auth for all API calls.
7. When expired, re-exchange the stored GitHub token for a fresh Copilot API token.

**Required Runtime Headers:**
```
Authorization: Bearer <copilot_api_token>
Copilot-Integration-Id: vscode-chat
Editor-Version: vscode/1.99.0
Editor-Plugin-Version: copilot-chat/0.26.7
User-Agent: GitHubCopilotChat/0.26.7
openai-intent: conversation-panel
x-github-api-version: 2025-04-01
```

**API Surface:**
- Base URL: `https://api.githubcopilot.com` (OpenAI-compatible).
- Model discovery: `GET https://api.githubcopilot.com/models` — returns dynamic model list based on subscription entitlement.
- Chat completions: `POST /chat/completions` (standard OpenAI format for most models).
- Claude-family models: route to `/v1/messages` (Anthropic format). Must strip `cache_control.ephemeral.scope` — Copilot rejects this Claude API extension field.
- GPT-5 Responses-capable models: route to `/responses` (except `gpt-5-mini` which stays on chat completions).
- Streaming SSE support.

**Implementation Notes for Local Router:**
- Provider ID: `github-copilot` (slug).
- Key env var: `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (the long-lived GitHub OAuth token, not the short-lived API token).
- Same OAuth token lifecycle challenge as Antigravity — needs `OAuthProviderState` with `{ githubToken, copilotApiToken, copilotApiTokenExpires }`.
- The `/config` UI needs a "Login with GitHub" device-flow button instead of a key text field.
- The Copilot device flow is simpler than Antigravity PKCE — no browser callback server needed, just terminal-based code entry. However, it has the extra step of exchanging the GitHub token for a Copilot API token.
- Important: The `Copilot-Integration-Id: vscode-chat` header is **required** on all API requests. Without it, GitHub returns `400 model_not_available_for_integrator: copilot-language-server` for newer models. This was a significant bug discovered and fixed in oh-my-pi PR #1210.
- Model routing logic needs to handle the split between `/chat/completions` (most models), `/v1/messages` (Claude models), and `/responses` (GPT-5 models) — currently Local Router only uses `/chat/completions` for all providers.
- The existing `custom-providers.json` cannot express these provider-specific routing rules. We may need a new `auth-providers.json` schema or extend `providers.txt` with auth type metadata.
- Credential dedup: oh-my-pi discovered that repeated logins accumulate duplicate credential rows because `ghu_`/`gho_` tokens are opaque (not JWTs). Fix: call `GET /api.github.com/user` after device flow to get the stable numeric GitHub user ID, use it as `accountId` for dedup. Local Router should implement this pattern from the start.
- Token storage: JetBrains IDEs store the Copilot OAuth token at `~/.config/github-copilot/apps.json`. We could optionally read this file for initial token discovery.

**Reference Implementations:**
- `oh-my-pi` / `pi-mono`: `npx @mariozechner/pi-ai login github-copilot` — full device flow with `loginGitHubCopilot()` function. PR #1210 added `Copilot-Integration-Id` header and credential dedup via `GET /api.github.com/user`. ([github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/1210](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/1210))
- Aider: Direct REST endpoint usage — set `OPENAI_API_BASE=https://api.githubcopilot.com` + `OPENAI_API_KEY=<oauth_token>`. Reads token from `~/.config/github-copilot/apps.json`. ([aider.chat/docs/llms/github.html](https://aider.chat/docs/llms/github.html))
- Conduit (Icehunter): Wire contract documented in `PROVIDER_COMPATIBILITY.md`. Covers device-code auth, token exchange, model discovery, runtime headers, Claude-family `/v1/messages` routing, and GPT-5 `/responses` routing. ([github.com/Icehunter/conduit/blob/main/PROVIDER_COMPATIBILITY.md](https://github.com/Icehunter/conduit/blob/main/PROVIDER_COMPATIBILITY.md))
- LiteLLM: Full Copilot provider with authenticator, model information, and test suite. ([litellm docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers/github_copilot))
- byterover-cli: Feature request #322 with detailed technical design for Copilot as first-class provider, including device flow, model discovery, provider registry entry, and scope of changes. ([github.com/campfirein/byterover-cli/issues/322](https://github.com/campfirein/byterover-cli/issues/322))
- forgiven: ADR 0004 documenting both LSP-side auth (device flow via `copilot-language-server`) and HTTP-side auth (agent panel token lifecycle with auto-refresh 60s before expiry). ([github.com/daneb/forgiven/blob/master/docs/adr/0004-copilot-authentication.md](https://github.com/daneb/forgiven/blob/master/docs/adr/0004-copilot-authentication.md))

### Shared Implementation Architecture

Both providers share a common challenge: **OAuth token lifecycle management** in a system currently designed for static API keys. The implementation plan:

1. **New TypeScript module: `src/oauth-providers.ts`**
   - `OAuthProviderState` interface: `{ provider: string, authType: 'oauth-pkce' | 'oauth-device', accessToken: string, refreshToken: string, expiresAt: number, accountId?: string }`
   - `loginAntigravity()` — PKCE flow: generate verifier/challenge, open browser, local callback server, token exchange.
   - `loginGitHubCopilot()` — Device flow: request device code, display code + URL, poll until authorized, exchange for Copilot API token, call `GET /api.github.com/user` for dedup.
   - `refreshOAuthToken(provider)` — Auto-refresh access tokens before expiry. For Copilot: re-exchange GitHub token for new API token. For Antigravity: use refresh token at Google OAuth endpoint.
   - `getOAuthApiKey(provider)` — Returns current valid access token, triggering refresh if needed. Drop-in replacement for `keyStore[provider]` reads.
   - Background refresh timer (check every 60s, refresh 5 minutes before expiry).

2. **PQC Bundle Extension**
   - Extend `secrets.bundle.json` payload to support `authType: 'oauth'` entries alongside existing static key entries.
   - OAuth entries store `{ authType, accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAt, accountId }` — all encrypted via AES-256-GCM + ML-KEM-768 as today.
   - The `pqc-secrets pack` / `pqc-secrets export` tools should be updated to handle OAuth entries, or the tokens should be managed entirely within the Local Router's own encrypted storage.

3. **Config UI Extension**
   - New "Login with..." buttons for OAuth providers (opens browser / displays device code).
   - Visual token status indicator (green = valid, yellow = expiring, red = expired, grey = not configured).
   - Quota usage display for Antigravity (if API provides it).

4. **Routing Integration**
   - New exhaustion tier: **Subscription OAuth** (between existing Subscription band and Paid band).
   - Quota-aware routing: detect 429 / quota-exhausted responses, temporarily deprioritize the provider.
   - The `providers.txt` catalog needs new metadata fields: `auth_type`, `oauth_provider`, `required_headers`.
   - New `providers.txt` entries:
     ```
     antigravity         | https://antigravity.googleapis.com/v1    | ANTAGRAVITY_OAUTH_TOKEN | oauth-pkce
     github-copilot      | https://api.githubcopilot.com            | COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN    | oauth-device
     ```

5. **Files to Create or Modify**
   - New: `src/oauth-providers.ts` — OAuth flows, token management, refresh logic.
   - New: `src/oauth-callback-server.ts` — Temporary HTTP server for PKCE callback (Antigravity).
   - New: `tests/oauth-providers.test.mjs` — Test suite for OAuth flows (mocked).
   - Modify: `src/index.ts` — Wire OAuth provider state into key resolution, add `/api/oauth/login/:provider` and `/api/oauth/status/:provider` endpoints.
   - Modify: `src/routes/config-api.ts` — OAuth login button handling, token status display.
   - Modify: `providers.txt` — Add `antigravity` and `github-copilot` provider entries with auth type metadata.
   - Modify: `src/routing-defaults.ts` — Add OAuth provider models to auto-router candidate lists.
   - Modify: `src/key-management.ts` — Extend key store to handle OAuth token state alongside static keys.
   - Modify: `src/ui/pages/providers.ts` — OAuth login UI components.
   - Modify: PQC secrets handling — Support `authType` discriminator in bundle payload.

## Child DOX Index

- [src/llms.txt](src/llms.txt) — TypeScript source: Express server, providers, routing, config API, UI renderers, streams, reasoning, PQC integration.
- [tests/llms.txt](tests/llms.txt) — MJS test contracts, integration fixtures, behavior boundaries.
- [scripts/llms.txt](scripts/llms.txt) — CI/CD and research scripts (MTS/MJS), model validation, catalog aggregation, CIP apply.
- [bin/llms.txt](bin/llms.txt) — Runtime entry points and CLI commands for local-router and PQC secrets.
- [build/llms.txt](build/llms.txt) — Compiled JS outputs from TypeScript; artifact boundary for production deploy.
- [community/llms.txt](community/llms.txt) — Public-facing contribution and community governance docs.
- [data/llms.txt](data/llms.txt) — Research manifests, CIP reports, benchmark sources, model catalog deltas, provider watch data.
- [.agents/llms.txt](.agents/llms.txt) — Operator task files, agent skills, research snapshots.
